newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end week lower but recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end week lower but recovery seen.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares closed the weak on Friday easier on continued profit taking but brokers said the bourse was likely to be boosted by a lower July inflation figure and World Bank's announcement that it would resume financial aid for the southern African country's economic reform programme.
The key industrial lost 88.40 points on Friday to close at 11,912.63, tumbling 122.88 points during the week.
"There are still some profit takers around but the lower inflation figure and the good news from the World Bank means more money coming to the stocks next week," one broker said.
Annual inflation dropped to 19.1 percent for the year to July from 21.4 percent in June.

Earlier on Friday, bourse officials said barring drought, Zimbabwe's share market should end the year at historic peaks, enthused by the World Bank's resumption of key aid to Harare after a two-year suspension.
"It will give a lot more confidence and optimism to the foreign investors," said Zimbabwe Stock Exchange chairmam Mark Tunmer.

Short-term interest rates on the local money market eased on Friday with dealers forecasting them to slip further on the back of the World Bank announcement coupled with the lower inflation figure, and stock market brokers said this should lead to more interest in equities.

The bourse's poor showing on Friday was on the back of a 200 cent drop to 4,000 in agricultural investors Chemco while tobacco company Rothmans shed 100 cents to 4,600 and hoteliers Meikles were down 50 cents at 3,050.

Others to trade weaker were pork producers Colcom which shed 30 cents to 450 while hotel group Zimsun at 525, tea and coffee growers EHPL at 225 and blue chip conglomerate Delta at 2,100 each lost 25 cents.
Minings continued lifeless with a 55 cent fall to 525 in nickel producer Bindura pushing the secondary index there 29.37 points lower to close at 894.17. It lost 23.79 points on the week.
